name: IL-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +19 partisan lean
Biss's large fundraising advantage over an underfunded Republican
Open seat after Schakowsky's retirement, but the seat remains safely Democratic
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 97%
model.rationale: The district's +19 Democratic lean and a fundamentals margin near 28 points make this a Safe D race despite the open seat. Daniel Biss has raised nearly $3 million while John Elleson has reported minimal resources, and markets price a Democratic win at 97%.
model.watch: A late surge of Republican outside spending or an unusually favorable national environment could narrow the margin, though a seat this Democratic is very unlikely to flip.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jan Schakowsky (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jan Schakowsky's retirement leaves this Chicago-area district open, but its strong Democratic lean of +19 points keeps the seat firmly in the party's column. Daniel Biss, a well-known local Democrat, enters the general election with a major financial edge, having raised nearly $3 million, while Republican John Elleson has reported little fundraising activity.

Outside groups have spent on both sides, but the district's fundamentals dominate. With no public polls available, the forecast rests on the partisan lean and the funding gap, both of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold. Prediction markets agree, pricing a Democratic win at 97%.
